# Platform, tooling and guards: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-PLAT-B13 | 2026-10-14 | Runtime design (architecture §5) as built in M13. The timer wheel has four levels of 256 one-millisecond slots (2^32 ms) and an overflow list; advance() jumps to the next tick where a slot fires or a non-empty slot cascades, so hours of timers cost no idle ticks; a handle carries a generation and a fired or cancelled timer's node is released before its callback runs. The inbox is a bounded ring with per-cell sequence numbers (lock-free MPSC); post() fails when full, and only the post that finds no wake pending writes the eventfd. The shard runs at most a ring's worth of tasks per wake, so timers and descriptors are not starved, brings the wheel up to the clock before any task runs, and arms the timerfd for the wheel's next deadline only; its start_timer() counts a delay from the clock, not from the wheel's last advance, so a timer is never early (the M13 CI run under TSan caught a 30 ms timer firing 1 ms early through the wheel's own schedule_in). The log façade formats with fmt and cannot format SecretBytes (a static_assert); quill can replace its sink later | src/platform/timer_wheel.hpp, src/platform/mpsc.hpp, src/platform/shard.hpp, src/platform/log.hpp, M13 |

Requests are a small binary format (version, op, length-prefixed fields; at most 1024 octets; a trailing octet is malformed): setup_node <netns> <parent> <addr>/<prefix>, teardown, socket <netns> sctp\|udp v4\|v6, list, gc. The policy: names ^ksim-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ up to 31 characters; a parent only the configured one, and none unless the host is kaluza-uesim (none on the dev PC); addresses only in the configured range (172.30.30.30-.39/24 in the lab); only namespaces netd lists may be torn down or have sockets made. setup_node makes a named namespace as iproute2 keeps them (a bind mount on /run/netns/<name>, made shared), lo up, and with a parent an L2 ipvlan 'ksim0' created straight into the namespace (IFLA_NET_NS_FD) carrying the address; a failure half way removes the namespace. socket makes the socket on a thread that joined the namespace and passes it over SCM_RIGHTS. ksim with a topology netd: section has netd make its CU-CP namespace and takes every NG-C socket from it through SctpClient's SocketSource; a socket keeps its namespace, so ksim binds and connects it in its own and never calls setns; the namespace goes at stop, and one left by a run that died is replaced | src/net/netd.cpp; src/net/netd_linux.cpp; src/net/netns.cpp; src/net/netlink.cpp; apps/ksim-netd; src/node/aio/aio.cpp; P1 N9 |

| KS-PLAT-B50 | 2026-10-16 | The PDCP fast path (P2 Q8). crypto::NeaContext and NiaContext key each AS algorithm once: NEA2 keeps one EVP AES-128-CTR context and resets its IV per PDU; NIA2 keeps OpenSSL's CMAC keyed and re-initialises it per message, fed in parts with no joined copy; NEA1/NIA1 keep the SNOW 3G key. A PDCP entity holds one of each per key. TX builds the PDU in one buffer sized once and ciphers in place. RX copies the PDU once, deciphers in place and checks the MAC-I over the header and data where they lie. A PDU in order with nothing buffered goes straight up without the reordering map (TS 38.323 5.2.2.1). The one-shot crypto::nea() and nia() run through the same contexts, so the known-answer sets check them. Measured (release, 1400 octets): NEA2 126 ns with its context against 386 ns keyed per packet, NIA2 608 against 1118 (KS-PLAT-T57). Of the plan's I/O items, the TUN read loop and recvmmsg were built in P1; sendmmsg moves to Q12, to be measured there first. | src/crypto/as_security.cpp; src/entity/pdcp/pdcp.cpp; tests/unit/crypto Kat.*; tests/unit/entity Pdcp.*; P2 Q8 |
